rows.ts_value: New $2.0bn 364-day senior revolving credit facility (single tranche, multicurrency), with a term-out option into term loans. Borrowers: Accenture Capital Inc., Accenture Global Capital DAC and Accenture Finance Limited. Guarantor: Accenture plc. Agent: Bank of America. To be documented in a new 364-Day Credit Agreement based on the Existing Credit Agreement of May 14, 2024.
rows.ts_quote: $2,000,000,000 364-DAY REVOLVING CREDIT FACILITY
rows.ca_value: New standalone 364-Day Credit Agreement dated April 22, 2026: a single multicurrency revolving facility with the same three Borrowers, Accenture plc as Guarantor and Bank of America, N.A. as Administrative Agent. Term-out by extending the maturity is in s.2.04(b). The CA also lets the Borrowing Agent add further Accenture Group 'Borrowing Affiliates' as Borrowers (s.2.13).

rows.explanation: The structure matches: a new standalone 364-day multicurrency revolver (not an amendment) with the same borrowers, guarantor and agent. The only addition is the s.2.13 mechanism for adding Borrowing Affiliates. The TS does not mention it, but it falls within the 'substantially similar to the Existing Credit Agreement' Documentation Principles.

rows.explanation: Most conditions match, but there are three minor differences that favour lenders. (1) The Extended Maturity Date of April 20, 2028 is 365 days after the April 21, 2027 Termination Date. That is one day earlier than the TS's 'one year after' the Initial Maturity Date (April 21, 2028, a Friday and a Business Day, so this is not a business-day adjustment; the gap arises because 2028 is a leap year). Total tenor is 729 days. (2) The CA adds a minimum 5-Business-Day notice period. (3) The TS excludes all reps 'relating to... litigation', but the CA excludes only s.5.06(b). Under the CA, s.5.06(a) must therefore still be true at term-out.

rows.explanation: The TS caps the combined increase amount at $2.0bn. The CA instead caps the combined total of both facilities at $9.5bn. The CA counts Five-Year commitments 'then in effect' (or outstanding Five-Year loans if those commitments have terminated), so headroom moves with the Five-Year Facility. The caps are equivalent only if combined commitments at closing are $7.5bn, which means a Five-Year Facility of $5.325bn alongside the $2.175bn 364-day amount. Neither document states the Five-Year size; the CA defines the Five-Year Credit Agreement as a new BofA-agented agreement dated as of the Closing Date. Recommend checking against that agreement. The $100m minimum, 10-Business-Day response period, no-Default condition and rep bring-down are covered by the TS only through its reference to the Existing Credit Agreement, which is not available to verify.

For USD loans only, ABR is the highest of WSJ prime, NYFRB + 0.50% and 1-month Term SOFR + 1.00%. All benchmarks (including Term CORRA itself, before the CSA is added) have a 0% floor and ABR has a 1.0% floor. ABR is available at 'the applicable Borrower's option'.

For CAD, the zero floor applies to the all-in Adjusted Term CORRA (Term CORRA plus CSA); the 'Term CORRA' definition itself has no floor. Base Rate is the greatest of WSJ Prime, NYFRB + 1/2 of 1% and 1-month Term SOFR + 1.00%, with a 1.00% floor. Daily Simple SOFR and Daily Simple CORRA apply only as s.3.03 fallbacks. (1) The CA bars Foreign Borrowers (the two Irish borrowers) from Base Rate Loans, while the TS offers ABR on any USD loan at each Borrower's option. This favours lenders and has practical effect. (2) The TS floors Term CORRA at 0% and adds the CSA on top, so the minimum CAD benchmark is the CSA. The CA floors only the all-in Adjusted Term CORRA at zero, so with negative CORRA the CA rate could be up to the CSA lower. This favours the borrowers but is remote. The direction shown is for difference (1). The Daily Simple SOFR/CORRA fallbacks are benchmark-replacement mechanics the Documentation Principles allow.

rows.ca_value: Section 7.01 negative pledge, which only catches Liens securing Indebtedness of the kinds in clauses (a), (b) or (e) of that definition (borrowed-money type) and related Guarantees. Permitted liens include: ordinary-course liens securing no more than US$20,000,000 per obligation; a general basket of 30% of Consolidated Total Assets; LC and statutory deposits; performance and bid bond liens; purchase money liens; and liens on acquired assets. Section 7.02(a) allows a merger only if the Guarantor (or a Borrower) survives with no Default. Section 7.02(b) prohibits a sale of all or substantially all of the assets of the Accenture Group taken as a whole, not of any single Loan Party's assets. There is no debt, restricted payment or investment covenant.
rows.ca_quote: (b) other Liens securing obligations in an aggregate principal or face amount at any time not to exceed an amount equal to 30% of the Consolidated Total Assets at such time
rows.explanation: The covenant categories match, but the scope is narrower than the TS wording. The TS limits sales of all or substantially all of 'its' assets, meaning each Borrower's and the Guarantor's. CA 7.02(b) tests only the Accenture Group taken as a whole, so one Borrower could sell all its assets without a breach. The negative pledge also covers only liens securing borrowed-money-type Indebtedness. The baskets (US$20m per ordinary-course lien, 30% of Consolidated Total Assets) are not in the TS and could not be checked, because the Existing Credit Agreement was not provided.

rows.attribute: Required lenders, voting and sacred rights
rows.ts_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of credit exposures and unused commitments. Consent of all affected Lenders is needed for: (i) commitment increases; (ii) reductions of principal, interest or fees; (iii) extensions of maturity or payment dates, except the Term-Out; (iv) release of the Guarantor; (v) changes to pro rata sharing or the waterfall, the Required Lenders definition and voting provisions, or the alternative currency provisions.
rows.ts_quote: require the approval of Lenders holding credit exposures and unused commitments representing more than 50% of the aggregate amount of credit exposures and unused commitments under the 364-Day Facility
rows.ca_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments, excluding Defaulting Lenders. Section 10.01(a) requires: (i) the affected Lender's consent to extend or increase its Commitment; (ii) each directly affected Lender to postpone payments, except the 2.04(b) term-out; (iii) each directly affected Lender to reduce principal, rate or fees, though Required Lenders alone can amend the Default Rate; (iv) every Lender for a change to Section 2.11 (sharing) or Section 8.03 (waterfall), but only one 'that would alter the pro rata sharing of payments'; (v) each affected Lender for Section 1.05 or the Alternative Currency definition; (vi) every Lender for voting provisions; (vii) every Lender to release Accenture plc. The AA must consent to changes affecting its rights, and Borrowing Affiliates are protected. Section 10.01(b) limits Defaulting Lender votes, lets the AA and Borrowing Agent correct errors, and allows an amend-and-restate that removes a fully paid-out Lender without its consent.
rows.ca_quote: Lenders having Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments representing in the aggregate more than 50% of the sum of the Revolving Exposures and unused Commitments of all Lenders at such time
rows.explanation: The voting threshold and all five TS sacred rights appear in the CA. One narrowing: the TS protects any modification to the pro rata sharing or waterfall provisions, but the CA protects changes to 2.11/8.03 only where they alter pro rata sharing. Required Lenders could therefore reorder the 8.03 waterfall. On the other hand, the CA needs every Lender, not just affected Lenders, for items (iv), (vi) and (vii). The CA also adds standard mechanics: Defaulting Lender exclusion, a Required-Lender-only Default Rate waiver, AA error correction, and Borrowing Affiliate protections.

TS: \"Exhibit B - Summary of Terms and Conditions\" to a Commitment Letter for a $2,000,000,000 364-Day Revolving Credit Facility for Accenture Capital Inc., Accenture Global Capital DAC and Accenture Finance Limited, guaranteed by Accenture plc. It is marked \"[CS&M Draft--03/26/2026]\" and has Addendum I (Fees and Interest Rates) on PDF pages 9-11. It is a formal term sheet. The closing date is left blank (\"April [], 2026\"). The TS says the CA will be based on the Existing Credit Agreement dated May 14, 2024 (JPMorgan as agent), subject to \"Documentation Principles\". The TS left-hand headings on PDF pages 2-6 are bunched together in the -layout text, but the body text order follows them.

It is not an amendment. s.10.22 (PDF page 129) waives the notice for terminating the Existing Credit Agreement. The companion Five-Year Credit Agreement is defined (PDF page 32) as a new agreement dated as of the Closing Date with Bank of America as agent.

(2) The TS pricing grid on PDF page 10 is jumbled in the -layout text file, and the PDF could not be rendered as an image (pdftoppm is not installed).
